- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 10–15% in the following 2–3 periods.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or oscillating), model often fails to revert to historical mean; adjust forecast toward 30-day rolling average of past 10–15 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (especially after 10–15 days), apply “downward bias correction” — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from positive to negative), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
